steps.claim: K=4096 bounds INT atoms only. The accepted 5u3 interpretation explicitly imposes no additional pointer-offset or memory-interval cardinality bound.
The measured D3 implementation closes more than 4096 pointer offsets even when EarlyChainClose is false, replacing them with a residue summary and adding EXT/top.
steps.by: witness:git -C ../bennett-plugin-rung4 show 0317dcf:src/Analysis.cpp, canonical(), OffsetChain=4096 and the unconditional t.total>OffsetChain branch

steps.claim: Reproduction: define an internal constant 8192-byte array filled with byte 1; an internal sink(ptr p) loads i8 from p; an internal action body calls sink with constant GEP offsets 0 through 4096; top enters that body through __bennett_adj. All addresses are in bounds. Run LLVM 18 opt with the saved p18-D3.so, -passes=bennett -bennett-dialect=0.2.10 -bennett-analysis-only -bennett-report=/dev/stdout -disable-output. I obtained INT(1), top=false with 4096 calls, but no atoms and top=true with 4097 calls.
PT9's finite pointer union and PT6's immutable-byte decoding require INT(1), top=false in both cases. There is no displacement cycle requiring acceleration.

steps.claim: The claims that the default follows K alone, that these are reference measurements, and that their growth is entirely spec-forced are therefore false. Matching D2/D3 states and delta checks do not repair this mismatch.

sol.fix: In note §§1–3 and §5, replace the reference claims with: 'The D-series runs used an additional non-reference closure after 4096 pointer offsets per provenance. Their logged sizes and timings describe that solver configuration, not the exact §5 reference least fixpoint. K bounds INT atoms only; no objects×4096 pointer-atom cap follows from the spec.' Either remove the unauthorised closure and rerun before claiming reference measurements, or retain the measurements with this corrected label and withdraw their reference-size conclusions. I would take the relabelling route now and select A. The conformance witness's expected load result is {INT(1)}, top=false at both 4096 and 4097 offsets.

steps.claim: PT6/PT7 preserve storage intervals and representation widths. ROOT provenance determines handle-use rejection, while disjoint ordinary fields remain ordinary data. The north star promises pointers, structs and handle collections without this additional restriction.
steps.by: clause:§5.2 PT6–PT7; clause:§6.2; clause:§6.4; clause:North Star §3.1 and §8

steps.claim: Option B collapses an 80-byte object after more than max(64,80/4)=64 store-created slots. Later access uses (X,*), and overlapping loads retain ROOT alternatives.
steps.by: witness:note §6 quoted amendment; witness:../bennett-plugin-rung4/src/Analysis.cpp store() and loadPair()

steps.claim: Reproduction on e-p:64:64-i64:64: top allocates [80 x i8] aligned to 8; allocates a one-wire handle h; stores h at offset 0 and i64 3 at offset 8; emits 63 separate i8 stores at offsets 16 through 78; stores h at offset 0 again; loads i64 n at offset 8; computes next=add i64 n,1; frees h and returns next. There are 65 distinct store-created intervals before the repeated handle store. Every access is valid and the integer field is disjoint from the handle field.

With -passes=bennett -bennett-dialect=0.2.10 -bennett-analysis-only -disable-output, the saved F2 plugin exits 0 by default: n={INT(0),INT(3)}, next={INT(1),INT(4)}, both without ROOT/top. Adding -bennett-analysis-early-chain-close exits 1 with 'BD-E-HANDLE-USE: §6.2 at %next = add i64 %n, 1'.

The measured rules introduce an actual source rejection, rather than merely greater cost or executable dispatch. Retaining ROOT names while discarding their field locations does not preserve scope. This remains a rejection under both dialect tracks' §6.2.

sol.fix: Replace note §6's recommendation and quoted B amendment with Option A and this rule: 'K applies only to INT atoms. The normative result remains the exact §5 least fixpoint. Representation changes MUST preserve storage intervals, representation widths, explicit ROOT/FN alternatives, reference verdicts, candidate sets and dispatch domains.' For the witness, require acceptance, ROOT(n)=empty, AV(n)={INT(0),INT(3)} and AV(next)={INT(1),INT(4)}. A second viable route is a redesigned B that retains exact ROOT intervals, requires exact-reference refinement before any newly proposed rejection, and supplies executable full-domain dispatch wherever precision is lost. That mechanism is absent here; I would take A.

codex.section: Note opening, §§2–3 and §5; dialect §5.1 and accepted 5u3 interpretation

steps.claim: K=4096 bounds INT atoms only. The accepted interpretation imposes no additional cardinality bound on pointer-offset sets or memory intervals and requires preservation of reference sets.
The measured implementation closes pointer sets beyond 4096 even when early-chain-close is false, adds EXT and sets top. The note nevertheless labels this mode the reference.

Construct a CC function containing qalloc/qfree, an internal global X of type [8193 x i8], and 4097 GEP values at offsets 2j for j=0..4096. Combine them with a balanced tree of pointer selects using an i1 parameter. Every offset is in bounds. PT2/PT3 require exactly (0 mod 2)[0,8193), with no EXT and top=false.

steps.claim: The reference retains storage intervals and representation widths. A disjoint integer field must not acquire handle provenance; only an actual handle-derived or partially overlapping handle access triggers BD-E-HANDLE-USE.
steps.by: clause:PT6–PT8; clause:§5.2 handle-array propagation requirement; clause:§6.2; clause:§6.4; clause:North Star §3.1

steps.claim: B collapses an object after more than max(64,extent/4) store-created slots and makes subsequent accesses use (X,*), retaining ROOT provenance.

On e-p:64:64, allocate X={ptr,[65 x i8]} and a clean one-wire handle h. Emit 65 separate stores of i8 1 at offsets 8+j, j=0..64; then store h at offset 0. Load i8 at offset 8, zero-extend it to i32, free h and return the integer. X has extent 80, so the threshold is 64. Its handle occupies [0,8); the loaded byte occupies [8,9), with no overlap.

Without early closing, the retained F2 binary accepts and reports AV(v)={INT(0),INT(1)}, top=false, with no ROOT. With -bennett-analysis-early-chain-close it exits 1: “BD-E-HANDLE-USE: §6.2 partial handle read” at the byte load.

This is an additional rejection of a supported, defined program, not merely an expensive executable dispatch domain. It is narrowing even though the widening is conservative for alias analysis and is disclosed.
steps.by: step:<2>1; step:<2>2; step:<2>3; step:<2>4; clause:binding no-narrowing rule

codex.fix: I would accept Option A. Replace note §6's recommendation with this exact text, retaining the equivalent accepted wording in dialect §5.1: “Retain the §5 reference analysis and the accepted 5u3 interpretation. K=4096 applies only to INT atoms; there is no additional cardinality cutoff for pointer-offset sets or memory intervals. Implementations MAY use exact symbolic sets, factored relations and SCC acceleration instead of enumeration, provided they preserve the reference least fixpoint, storage intervals, representation widths, explicit ROOT and FN alternatives, verdicts, candidate sets and dispatch domains. An implementation time or memory cap reports an unfinished build with the exhausted resource and leaves the implementation obligation open; it does not authorize source rejection or a runtime fault. Unmodified SQLite remains required. All non-exact closing, including the current 4096-pointer-offset rule, remains a non-reference experiment.” For the witness, require accept, AV(v)={INT(0),INT(1)}, no ROOT, and concrete return 1. The other viable route is a redesigned B with this additional rule: “Summary-created overlap MUST NOT establish handle use or escape; retain the original interval-sensitive reference result for those checks. Loss of finite non-handle information MUST have an accepted executable lowering; where that lowering is unavailable, retain the original reference domains rather than reject, block or fault because of widening.” That route needs a separately specified semantic revision and cannot be obtained merely by loosening the constants. I choose A.
